item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) The Abnormal High School
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Action

Elevator Pitch: twenty-five (25) humanoids, thirteen (13) male humanoids, and twelve (12) female humanoids that're infected by an unknown phenomenon in an abandoned high school that turns them into mutants with dangerous abilities.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX, also known as "The Abnormal High School," is a high-school located somewhere deep in the woods, abandoned due to the place where it was being built was used as a testing zone for nuclear weapons of the government. In the year 2006, twenty-five individuals who are runaways had entered the school as they experienced a mysterious headache that causes them to faint for a long time after they were awake; they've discovered that they're not normal anymore, or to be specific; they have become something that cannot be explained. SCP-XXXX was brought to the Foundation's attention when they've received witness reports of a boy levitating in the middle of the air, at the same time altering the wind, as they've discovered that the humanoid male is located in an area with nuclear waste. This resulted in dispatching as Task-Force MTF Beta-7 as they were a success in retrieving all of the subjects that're in SCP-XXXX

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The origins of SCP-XXXX trace back to the early 19s. A mysterious asteroid landed into the abandoned high-school after it was tested by the government's nuclear weapons, which the school was completely obliterated into oblivion. However, with the asteroid's presence, it has been reconstructed back as new.

Additional Notes: Hope you enjoy it.

Forum thread: SCP-5083

Some day "I can fix this" will be uttered by a character undergoing a crisis, and they will be able to fix whatever this is. Today is not that day.

Very well done, overall. Compelling action, good call-backs, oodles of character development, and some interesting turns that, while not out of left field, still feel surprising. With halfway left for the rest of this cycle, I am very, very interested to see where it goes, in a way that I haven't been for a series in some time.

My one complaint is that the description of various characters is so distinctive that it's very obvious when you are cribbing from previous works, sometimes word for word (Medea has "shoulder-length brunette hair and faint blue eyes"; Jason has "mop of curly blond hair; Jeffery is "a middle-aged man with dark skin"; Anderson has "triangular grating that rapidly hissed with the passage of air" and "two small camera lenses that glowed with a faint green light"). They aren't bad descriptions, but it was a shame to be jerked out of the narrative several times by the realization that "hey, wait, didn't Conwell already say this?"

Still, an easy +1

item.title: A helping hand (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP involves a floating hand which assists people with things when they are needed, the SCP teleports to anyone who says they need help with something, this will not work if they are only thinking of needing help and not saying it,

Central Narrative: The hand is cut off at the wrist area, the inside shows a black void.
Testing showed that it can only help with things if it's within a 5 meter radius and will help with anything it can, it can hammer a nail in the wall, or shoot a target as long as it's within 5 meters of the person needing help.

It is able to teleport anywhere on the world and wont stay any longer than needed so containment isn't possible and has since been classified as Keter, it's presence was noticed by the foundation in 2011 when a twitter user Robert Hexain posted a message about the SCP who helped him repair his roof.

When there are multiple people in need of assistance it will randomly choose one to help and will help the other later if they still need help, during testing a tracker was put on the SCP to locate it at all times to see who the SCP helped, they will then be tracked down, interviewed and given Class B amnestics

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It can be helpful or it can be really dangerous

item.title: Re: SCP Idea (Seeking Greenlight): Elaine of Astolat's Curse
item.content:encoded:
This feels somewhat reminiscent of SCP-4205 in the way that the people affected by the anomaly react and like, what happens to them; and I'm not exactly sure how this ties into Elaine of Astolat.

Really my biggest concern with this, narratively speaking, is it feels very passive: there's not really any kind of narrative stakes or anything pulling the story forward; so it ends up feeling very flat. It feels like there really needs to be more of an indication of how the increase in -1 occurrences is causing the Foundation to more and more desperately look into this.

It also feels very flat: there's not a lot of growth or change between the start of the story and the end, and the only real difference I can see is that everyone knows more about what is going. It really feels like it needs something permanent to happen here: for the SCP to understand what is happening and change as a result, or for the Foundation to find stuff out and react by changing containment procedures or doing new experiments or something.

item.title: Re: The No-Tell Motel
item.content:encoded:
Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, (Some) Comedy, Sci-Fi

Page Layout (Optional): Article Format

Elevator Pitch:

⦁ A seemingly unassuming small hotel in the Mojave Desert

⦁ The interior is infinitely larger than the exterior

⦁ The motel is a fixed point in multiple realities

⦁ There's no observable staff from outside, but inside there is

⦁ Those who have seen the staff cannot recall any physical features, only that they are polite and courteous

⦁ Some staff have personalities that can be recalled, but that is the only memorable trait they have

⦁ Those who stay past check out are escorted out by security, also whose features are unable to be recalled

⦁ Occasionally, those that check in are altered to have an anomalous ability/property, and it is hinted by the staff that that's one of the reasons why they are drawn in

⦁ The halls are infinite and labyrinthine

⦁ The motel rooms are generic and normal-seeming

⦁ The motel room windows each look out on different worlds

⦁ Some people who leave the motel are from alternate Earths

⦁ Despite the monitoring and security, somehow, sometimes some people manage to get past to check in

⦁ An exploration log will be included, detailing science teams with armed escorts as well as D-class personnel teams exploring the Motel's interior

⦁ A breach log which will detail instances where civilians attempt to gain entry to the site, have gained entry, as well as those who managed to make it into the motel. This log will also include instances where those who entered are recovered. It will also detail instances where on-site personnel themselves attempted to check in to the motel.

Central Narrative: World-building

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The motel occasionally has a guest who stays in a room that looks out onto our world, and the dressers are filled with money from different time periods and countries, some of which no longer exist or have never existed. And the money includes ancient drachmas, crudely carved red painted stones, and etc.

Additional Notes: I'm not sure where I need help, but I gladly accept any advice willing to be given!

item.title: Re: SCP-5832
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

I'm not really a fan of the narrative you're setting out here; and the idea of a tiny paper town is something of a cliche; so I'm really not convinced by this idea as a whole.

This said: if you can figure out an interesting story to tell about the two castles and their interactions, and a good way to really get the foundation into the perspective of the factions so you can really show the internal strife, this could be interesting.

Alternatively: maybe this would read a lot better as a 'tale' consisting of e.g. diary entries say from a member of the original town: really like, showing the coming into foundation containment angle and the war with the other castle that way, and having a big character arc, perhaps where the two castles realise that each other aren't the enemy but the foundation are since the foundation is keeping them locked up and working to prevent their growth and stuff.

Either way: the conflict between the two castles feels like it's meant as the central conflict of the article but the summary here completely glazes over it to the point where it almost feels more like an after thought to add interest rather than a well developed angle.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hi everyone!

I love creative stories and heard about the SCP a few months ago. After looking at the site and reading both old and new articles, I can see that this is something really special. In a way, the stories here give me the same sense of awe and wonder I get when reading about ancient Egyptian or Greek mythology, except with a special 21st-century internet twist. I have an idea or two for an SCP article, and it would be an honor to have it accepted someday (after many, many rounds of feedback and rewrites of course:))

One thing that keeps me up at night is probably the inner workings of how we communicate. Language is so complex, yet I sometimes find myself struggling to find how best to phrase an idea or viewpoint.

I'm very excited to be a part of this community, and I hope I'll get to know many of you as we add to this pantheon of the 21st century!

item.title: A video game that kills REVISION (seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

  • The SCP is a video game cartridge with scratched up stickers and a scratched logo and title which is impossible to make out.
  • a video game cartridge that can be played on Nintendo 64, but no one1 remembers or knows about the game or the development of the game.
  • whenever a player dies in the video game, within 24 hours the player in real life would face the same fate as the player who died in the video game.

Central Narrative:
The SCP itself has no unusual properties and can be handled with ease, just simply, anyone can touch it, bite it, whatever. The SCP starts to act strange when the SCP is plugged into a Nintendo 64 console.

The SCP is a game cartridge with scratched-up stickers, there is no title but does have a brand name called "PlugSoft"2.

Important information about the thing: When the cartridge is plugged into a regular Nintendo 64, the player will be introduced into an open-world. When the player starts, the subject will appear to be in a trance focusing on the game ignoring anything like pain and loud noises, if the SCP is plugged out or the subject is removed from the screen the subject will immediately be in a hostile state killing anyone who interfered, and after killing, the subject will kill (him/her)self. The place that sets the player is a city called: "Alterio City", the player inside the game can virtually do ANYTHING3. Whenever the player dies, the subject will instantly die as the same fate.4

The SCP item was created by a 19-year-old male Korean programmer, possibly a PlugSoft developer, and wanted to make a game that gave people a city with no rules. The programmer was found dead5 with a note on his left hand. The note read about the programmer fighting depression and stress, and couldn't take anymore.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: What is special about this SCP is because I think (I THINK! I am not certain) that this SCP is the first video game that kills anyone. (Again, I am not certain, there is probably an SCP like this. I don't know…)

Additional Notes: I would LOVE! to see some criticism or feedback. Thank you!

Footnotes
1. as in people in a video game developing companies, as well as Nintendo
2. The PlugSoft is a video game company that produces anomalous 'video games.'
3. in that, they can commit any crime easily
4. if a player died of a car crash, the subject in the real world will die with the same injuries in the game
5. suicide, a gun was found on his right hand

item.title: Re: Shepherd boy
item.content:encoded:
► my detailed thoughts◄
- close

SCP-XXXX is to be stored in Containment Area M21 located in 300m underground of the Gobi desert in Mongolia.

Delete that second “in” (right before 300m)

SCP-XXXX is to be held in a 5 m cube made of entirely Tungsten metal, with no gap for organic life to enter.

Why does it matter that the cube be Five meters in length/widtch/height? What if it were 4.98 meters? Would that invalidate the containment? This is why specific measurements of containment chambers is mostly avoided these days.

If any entities that reside in SCP-XXXX-1 move from their position, they are to be immediately apprehended and interrogated before being held in a cell with same containment procedure as SCP-CXXX.

Suggest: Entities residing in SCP-XXXX-1 that move from their position, are to be apprehended, interrogated, and remanded to a containment cell under equivalent containment procedures as SCP-XXXX.

No more than five personnel wearing Hazmat suits, are to enter SCP-XXXX-1 at the same time. Its activity is to be monitored 24/7 and no unauthorized personnel and civilian are to be in the proximity of the area or enter SCP-XXXX-1.

Suggest: A maximum of five hazmat protected personnel are permitted to enter SCP-XXXX-1 at any given time. Access to SCP-XXXX-1 is restricted to security cleared personnel.

In the event of a Containment Breach, all on site researchers and personnel are to evacuate immediately or stay in shelter until the MTF Theta-4 (“Gardeners”) arrive at the facility and apprehended the entity.

Suggest: In the event of a containment breach, all on-site personnel are to evacuate or shelter in place until such time as MTF-Theta-4 (“Gardeners”) apprehend the entity.

ALSO: which entity? Clarify

SCP-CXXX consists of two components: a cave (SCP-XXXX-1) and humanoid protecting it (SCP-XXXX).

Suggest: SCP-XXXX consists of two interrelated anomalies: a cave, designated as SCP-XXXX-1 and a humanoid entity guarding the cave, designated as SCP-XXXX.
ALSO: I suggest reversing the designations, the Cave could be the XXXX and the humanoid, -1, because it seems the cave is the central anomaly.

SCP-XXXX is a Hun male, its skin is olive-brown from sunburn and wears an old dark green Hun area deel1 which been ripped and torn, however, SCP-XXXX refused to change it.

SCP-XXXX has the ability to manifest entities made out of natural components which resemble a Chinese dragon. Entities length is unknown.
So several things, “an old dark green Hun area deel” is confusing… suggest: “SCP-XXXX is a Hun male, its skin is olive-brown from sun damage and an deteriorating, dark-green Hun deel that the entity refuses to change.” & I don’t know what “made out of natural components” means in this context, so I would clarify.

ALSO: IS this meant to be two paragraphs? If so, there is no spacing between them.

SCP-XXXX-1 is a cave under abandoned Mining factory, it is measured to be around 6 kilometers deep.

Suggest: a cave under an abandoned mining facility, measured to be approximately six kilometers below the surface.

However, how big SCP-XXXX-1 mass is impossible to measure. SCP-XXXX-1 resides a snake-like creature approximately 1 kilometers, maybe even bigger.

Suggest: Exact measurements of SCP-XXXX-1’s dimensions have been impossible due to a large serpentine entity, at least one kilometer in length, that resides within the cave.

About fifty kilometers down, there is a massive field stretching further from the human eye, filled with stationary humanoids varies in ages, they're made out of natural components, different species of flowers but growing in the same root. The radio cuts off the moment entering SCP-XXXX-1.

Fifty kilometers down where? I thought you said the cave was 6 km below the surface? What do you mean? Also this is just really awkwardly written.

The investigation into SCP-XXXX-1 and its relation with SCP-XXXX is ongoing.

Cut this. It’s implied because there’s more to read after it.

This is a critique in progress… You have so many awkward phrases and poorly structured sentences… I would sit down and really examine your work here, and see if you can't clean it up without myself or another critter to do so.

item.title: SCP Idea: Stuck in the Past
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: Basically, it's a set of three anomalous access dial-up Internet access numbers, each with the same anomalous property: when you connect to it, your web browser is pretty much transported back to the late 2000s. Everything is as it was back then: web sites, web services, social media are all unchanged from their original forms back then, and it can all be interacted with by users of this SCP. For all intents and purposes, this SCP is a type of time machine.

Central Narrative: The Foundation discovers the existence of this SCP in 2017, and a few years later they use it to interview some people from the past. Through these interviews, they discover the possible origin of the SCP, and eventually they find one of its' creators. He explains how it was made and why it was made (making reference to an unnamed made-up SCP with time and reality manipulation powers which the foundation has not yet contained, cuz im too lazy to find an existing SCP matching those criteria :P)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: There are many internet-based SCPs, but I have yet to see one which is directly affiliated with the internet itself rather than just using it as a medium through which to do its "thing". The internet is a big and scary place, and I feel like its many different subcultures and groups (and its history) have so much potential as a source of inspiration for SCPs. After all, without the internet, the Foundation wouldn't exist ;)

Additional Notes: I've already typed up a draft of the entire article + the chat/interview logs, if you want me to post it here I can.

Thanks for reading my idea, everyone! This is my second real SCP idea that I've posted here, and it's the first one that I'm really, truly super proud of ^u^ It's been such a long time, I honestly forgot how much I love writing…

item.title: Re: A joke SCP about amnestics (Seeking greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
I was summoned by PM. Let's do this!

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

First of all, I want to clarify that humor is subjective (I laugh with almost everything), so I might not be able to tell if people will like this or not. I'll give you crit from my point of view.

A club classified as an SCP-J by the CKG Gathering due to its ability to erase memories

I think this would be the second article regarding the CKG Gathering, so there's almost nothing about CKG's lore. You may or may not expand it, but you'll need to explain some things here: Why do the CKG want to erase memories? What's the object class? What are their "protocols" for the usage of the club?

will subvert the reader's expectation by revealing the Foundation simply decided to use other tools to bash heads

You can achieve this by constantly calling them "amnestics", and then revealing a photo of an aluminium bat(And I think that would be really funny, ngl). But I'm concerned about the way you're going to write the article. Are you going to add interviews, reports, test logs…? Of course, they all would be in the 'CKG format', but I want to know what kind of layout you're going to use, especially to display the modern version of the object.

Also, while I like the idea of hitting someone in the head to erase their memory, I feel like this is a little… sour. I think you should add some kind of story to it, even a little one. Maybe they were using the same guy for all the tests and they had comedic reactions? Maybe some people used the object by accident? Maybe the CKG kept using it on each other by accident or something?

Overall, I really like this idea, but humor is very subjective, so I'll suggest reaching out to other reviewers to see their opinions.

Feel free to contact a member of the Butterfly Squad to get more crit, or PM me to take another look!

Because like, I think prisons are bad? I think locking up people is bad and I'm not really interested in how jailers perceive themselves, they're still jailers. They may think they're doing necessary evils and all but at the bottom of their beliefs is (ostensibly) a desire to maintain the Veil and I couldn't disagree with them more.

But yeah, like, the versions the SH that are more obviously flawed in the ways you describe are pretty cool; I do wish they had more consistent characterization.
